title: The load brake runs on the cloud too, with a remedy that works there
why: Owner glossary ruling topic 1, 14:36 CST Nov 10.
note: Glossary topic 1 close (owner 14:36 CST Nov 10): remove rule-chosen local/cloud splits. Plan (opus) and refuter 14:54 CST: drop is_cloud() from load_hit, running_agent_hit and lane_session_hit (guard.py ~3901, ~3952, ~3971); guard_log_report.py prints a reading in place of n/a (cloud), and CLAUDE.md reports-batch-pace-numbers changes with it; create_session keeps its skip as a forced split (the new session runs in another container). Refuter gap: the refusal remedies (LOAD_FULL_REASON 'wait, then retry'; parent frees space) strand a cloud session, whose disk does not drain while it waits; the tool needs a cloud steer. Departs from owner 2026-11-01 21:34 CST (brake local-only, machine-load-brake.md:20), which the 14:36 ruling covers. Red: test_guard.py load-brake family with CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true and an injected full read_load. After #2566 merges (CLAUDE.md:106 is one line that both rewrite). Blocker glossary-roles-g1-g3 cleared 13:55 CST Nov 12: it has no step file; its branch merged (0f01d4249) and #2566 is on main (50bf06b2a) (lane glossary-same-local-cloud). Lane glossary-same-local-cloud 13:53 CST Nov 12, held for a go: on a cloud container read_load() gives memory_pct None (no Linux memory reader) and disk 29.7 GB free of 252 GB, but a cloud disk is a per-session allowance, so dropping is_cloud() gives a brake that never fires or fires on a wrong reading. Proposal: measure the cloud allowance first, add a Linux memory read and a cloud-aware disk read (red first), then drop is_cloud(). The Nov 10 14:36 ruling allows a forced split inside the tool.
